title: Prevalence of Listeria monocytogenes in Ewe Milk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
content: Listeria monocytogenes, a foodborne pathogen of global concern, poses significant health risks through the consumption of contaminated dairy products, including ewe milk. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the prevalence of L. monocytogenes in ewe milk, considering regional, methodological, and seasonal variations, and to identify potential risk factors contributing to contamination.The study systematically reviewed peer-reviewed articles and research papers published from 2000 to 2024. Data were extracted from studies employing standard microbiological and molecular techniques for the detection of L. monocytogenes in raw and processed ewe milk samples. The meta-analysis synthesized prevalence rates across diverse geographical regions, emphasizing differences between developed and developing countries.Results reveal a pooled global prevalence rate of L. monocytogenes in ewe milk, highlighting significant variability based on sampling methods and regional practices. Higher prevalence rates were observed in regions with inadequate hygienic practices during milking and processing, underscoring the importance of improved food safety measures. Seasonality also played a critical role, with increased prevalence during warmer months due to enhanced bacterial growth conditions. Furthermore, molecular characterization of isolates demonstrated considerable genetic diversity, suggesting multiple contamination sources and transmission pathways.The findings emphasize the need for stringent monitoring programs, adherence to hygienic milking practices, and implementation of pasteurization in high-risk regions to mitigate the public health risks associated with L. monocytogenes. Future research should focus on advanced detection techniques and interventions to reduce contamination in the dairy supply chain.
